en: being about the same; looking alike

examples.en: The two of them are about the same height.

examples.ko: 우리 반 아이들 성적은 대부분 엇비슷한 편이에요.
examples.en: Most of the kids in our class have about the same grades.

examples.ko: 두 가게 가격이 엇비슷해서 고르기 어려워요.
examples.en: The prices at the two shops are so similar that it's hard to choose.
Those brothers look pretty much alike.

examples.ko: 두 팀의 실력이 엇비슷하면 경기가 더 재미있어요.
examples.en: A game is more fun when the two teams are evenly matched.
My idea was about the same as my friend's.

explain: '비슷하다'보다 두 쪽의 차이가 거의 없다는 느낌이 강해서 키, 실력, 가격처럼 견줄 수 있는 것에 잘 어울려요. '~와/과 엇비슷하다', '엇비슷하게'처럼 비교하는 말과 함께 써요. 말할 때 '비슷하다'로 바꿔도 자연스러워요.
explain_en: It feels stronger than '비슷하다' (similar) in that there is almost no difference, so it suits things you can compare, such as height, skill and price. It is used with a comparison, as in '~와/과 엇비슷하다' or '엇비슷하게'. In speech you can also swap in '비슷하다' and still sound natural.

examples.en: I half-rose from my chair and greeted them.
The child stood there awkwardly and looked at the teacher.

examples.ko: 버스가 갑자기 서서 사람들이 엉거주춤 휘청거렸어요.
examples.en: The bus stopped suddenly and people staggered in awkward half-crouches.

examples.ko: 그는 엉거주춤 무릎을 구부리고 신발 끈을 묶었어요.
examples.en: He bent his knees halfway and tied his shoelaces.

examples.ko: 엉거주춤 서 있지 말고 편하게 앉으세요.
examples.en: Don't stand there half-bent, just sit down and relax.

examples.ko: 그는 엉거주춤 손을 내밀다가 도로 거뒀어요.
examples.en: He hesitantly reached out his hand and then pulled it back.

explain: 앉지도 서지도 않은 어정쩡한 자세를 말할 때 쓰고, '서다·일어나다·앉다' 같은 동작과 자주 같이 나와요. 몸짓뿐 아니라 마음을 정하지 못한 태도에도 비유로 쓸 수 있어요.
explain_en: It describes an in-between posture, neither fully sitting nor standing, and often appears with verbs like '서다', '일어나다' and '앉다'. It can also be used figuratively for an undecided attitude, not just body posture.

examples.en: I tried to get up from the chair but froze in a half-risen position.

examples.ko: 모두 자리에 앉는데 저만 엉거주춤하게 서 있었어요.
examples.en: Everyone was sitting down, and only I was standing there awkwardly.

examples.ko: 어떻게 할지 몰라서 한참 엉거주춤하고 있었어요.
examples.en: I didn't know what to do, so I hovered awkwardly for a while.
I wasn't sure whether to greet them, so I hesitated awkwardly.

examples.ko: 엉거주춤해 보이길래 제가 의자를 빼 드렸어요.
examples.en: You looked awkwardly half-bent, so I pulled out the chair for you.
If you stand half-bent on a bus, you can easily fall.

explain: '엉거주춤하게 서 있다', '엉거주춤한 자세'처럼 뒤의 말을 꾸미는 모양으로 자주 써요. 부사 '엉거주춤'과 뜻은 같고, 몸의 자세뿐 아니라 어찌할지 몰라 머뭇거리는 상태에도 써요.
explain_en: It is often used to modify what follows, as in '엉거주춤하게 서 있다' or '엉거주춤한 자세'. It means the same as the adverb '엉거주춤' and covers both an awkward body posture and a hesitant, unsure state.

examples.en: Before I knew it, I had said 'yes'.
I was startled and screamed without thinking.
On instinct, I grabbed my friend's hand and ran.
In my confusion, I ended up handing over my wallet.
My name was called suddenly, and I stood up without thinking.
I said it on the spur of the moment, so I regret it now.

explain: 거의 '엉겁결에' 모양으로만 써요. 놀라거나 당황해서 생각할 틈 없이 한 행동에 쓰고, 별 생각 없이 한 행동에 쓰는 '무심코'와는 당황한 느낌이 있다는 점이 달라요.
explain_en: It is used almost only in the form '엉겁결에'. It fits actions done without time to think because you were surprised or flustered, which differs from '무심코' (without really thinking), which has no sense of panic.

examples.en: My hair got tangled because of the wind.
The thread is so tangled that I can't undo it.

examples.ko: 이어폰 줄이 가방 안에서 엉클어져 있어요.
examples.en: The earphone cord is all tangled up inside my bag.
I combed my messy, tangled hair.
Let's sort things out quickly before the situation gets messy.
Be careful so the fishing line doesn't get tangled.

explain: 머리카락, 실, 줄처럼 길고 가는 것이 뒤죽박죽 얽힐 때 써요. '헝클어지다'라고도 하고, 일이나 관계가 복잡하게 꼬일 때 비유로도 써요.
explain_en: It is used when long, thin things like hair, thread and cords get jumbled and knotted. People also say '헝클어지다', and it can be used figuratively when a task or relationship gets complicatedly tangled.

examples.ko: 저 사람은 웃고 있지만 속은 엉큼해요.
examples.en: That person is smiling, but is sly inside.
You look gentle, but you're surprisingly sly.
Don't slyly eavesdrop on other people's conversations.

examples.ko: 엉큼해 보이는 사람은 조심하는 게 좋아요.
examples.en: It's better to be careful around people who seem sly.

examples.ko: 그 사람, 알고 보니 꽤 엉큼했어요.
examples.en: As it turned out, that guy was quite devious.
I noticed his sly motive and turned him down.

explain: 겉으로는 모르는 척하면서 속으로 딴생각이나 꿍꿍이를 품은 사람에게 써서 칭찬이 아니에요. '음흉하다'와 비슷하게 쓰이고, 상황에 따라 이성에게 흑심이 있다는 느낌으로 들릴 수 있으니 조심해서 써요.
explain_en: It describes someone who pretends not to know while hiding other thoughts or schemes, so it is never a compliment. It is used much like '음흉하다', and depending on context it can sound like someone has improper romantic intentions, so use it with care.

examples.en: It rained a lot last evening.
I've had a headache since last evening.
Did you watch the news last evening?
I watched a movie with a friend last evening.
The food I ate last evening was really good.
I was tired last evening, so I fell asleep early.

explain: '어제저녁'을 줄인 말이라 어제 저녁만 가리켜요. 비슷하게 생긴 '엊그제'(그저께나 며칠 전)와 헷갈리지 마세요. 말할 때 편하게 쓰는 느낌이에요.
explain_en: It is a shortened form of '어제저녁', so it refers only to yesterday evening. Don't confuse it with the similar-looking '엊그제' (the day before yesterday or a few days ago). It has a casual, spoken feel.

examples.en: The two teams traded the lead back and forth.

examples.ko: 어젯밤에는 걱정돼서 엎치락뒤치락 잠을 못 잤어요.
examples.en: I was worried last night and tossed and turned without sleeping.
The kids rolled around playing on the bed.
First and second place kept swapping ranks.

examples.ko: 요즘 인기 순위가 엎치락뒤치락 계속 바뀌어요.
examples.en: The popularity rankings keep flipping back and forth these days.

examples.ko: 선거 결과는 엎치락뒤치락 끝까지 알 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The election was so back and forth that we couldn't know the result until the end.

explain: 뒤집히고 바뀌는 모습을 나타내서, 경기나 순위에서 서로 앞서거니 뒤서거니 할 때와 잠을 못 자고 이리저리 뒤척일 때 둘 다 써요. 동작을 말할 때는 '엎치락뒤치락하다'로도 써요.
explain_en: It shows things flipping and swapping, so it is used both when competitors keep overtaking each other in a game or ranking and when someone tosses and turns unable to sleep. As an action it also appears as '엎치락뒤치락하다'.

en: toss about; have a close game

examples.en: The two players traded the lead and finally tied.
The class rankings flip-flop with every exam.
I was worried and tossed and turned all night.
It was such a back-and-forth game that I watched to the end.
The two candidates keep overtaking each other.

examples.ko: 강아지 두 마리가 바닥에서 엎치락뒤치락하며 놀아요.
examples.en: Two puppies play, rolling over each other on the floor.

explain: 경기나 선거처럼 서로 앞서고 뒤바뀌는 접전에 쓰고, 순위가 계속 오르내릴 때도 써요. 잠을 못 자고 뒤척일 때는 '뒤척이다'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is used for close contests like games and elections where the lead keeps changing, and also when rankings keep going up and down. For tossing and turning in bed, people also say '뒤척이다'.

examples.en: Aw, you left your umbrella behind again?
Aw, how hard it must be, having caught a cold.
Oh dear, how could you say it like that?
Oh my, you've already finished it all?
Ugh, you're going to be the death of me!

examples.ko: 에이그, 숙제도 안 하고 놀고만 있어요.
examples.en: Tsk, you're just playing without doing your homework.

explain: 못마땅하거나 안쓰럽거나 답답할 때 혼잣말처럼 나오는 소리예요. 상대에게 크게 화내기보다 한숨 섞인 아쉬움을 나타내고, 비슷한 상황에서 '아이고'도 써요.
explain_en: It is a sound that slips out like a mutter when you are displeased, sympathetic or exasperated. It expresses sighing disappointment rather than real anger at someone, and '아이고' can be used in similar situations.

examples.en: That person is no pushover.

examples.ko: 새로 온 팀장님이 여간내기가 아니라서 긴장돼요.
examples.en: The new team leader is formidable, so I'm nervous.

examples.ko: 저 가게 사장님은 여간내기가 아닌 것 같아요.
examples.en: That shop owner seems like no ordinary person.

examples.ko: 동생이 여간내기가 아니라서 아무도 못 속여요.
examples.en: My younger sibling is so sharp that nobody can fool them.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 여간내기는 아니니까 조심해야 해요.
examples.en: That player is no easy opponent, so we have to be careful.
I heard that she's quite a formidable person.

explain: 거의 '여간내기가 아니다'처럼 부정과 함께 써서, 만만치 않고 보통 사람과 다르다는 말이 돼요. 능력이 뛰어나서 감탄할 때도, 상대하기 까다로워서 경계할 때도 써요.

phrases.en: The new teacher is no pushover.
phrases.nuance_ko: '보통 사람이 아니다'라는 말을 그대로 풀면 되지만, 실제로는 능력이 대단하거나 만만치 않다는 감탄·경계를 담은 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: It literally says 'not an ordinary person', but in practice it is a set phrase carrying admiration or wariness about someone formidable.

explain_en: It is almost always used with a negative, as in '여간내기가 아니다', meaning someone is not to be underestimated. It can express admiration for someone's ability or wariness about someone hard to deal with.

examples.en: She is called a heroine of the political world.
I read stories about heroic women in history.
The heroine of that movie is a bold, spirited woman.
My grandmother was known as a strong woman in the village.

examples.ko: 여걸 소리를 들을 만큼 배짱이 있어요.
examples.en: She has enough nerve to be called a heroine.
One heroic woman appears in the novel.

explain: 배짱과 능력이 뛰어나서 남자 못지않다는 칭찬으로 쓰는 말이에요. 주로 글이나 이야기에서 만나고, 보통 '여걸로 불리다', '여걸 소리를 듣다'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It is praise for a woman with great nerve and ability, as capable as any man. You mostly meet it in writing and stories, usually in patterns like '여걸로 불리다' or '여걸 소리를 듣다'.

examples.en: In the past, there were many women working in factories.

examples.ko: 어머니는 젊을 때 방직 공장 여공이셨어요.
examples.en: My mother was a textile factory worker when she was young.
I watched a documentary about female factory workers.

examples.ko: 그 시대 여공들은 힘든 환경에서 일했어요.
examples.en: Female factory workers of that era worked in hard conditions.

examples.ko: 여공 생활을 한 할머니가 이야기해 주셨어요.
examples.en: A grandmother who had lived as a factory girl told us her story.
I read a book about the lives of female factory workers in the 1970s.

explain: 주로 산업화 시기의 공장에서 일하던 여성을 가리키는 역사적인 느낌의 말이에요. 요즘 일터의 여성에게는 '여성 노동자'나 '여직원'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: It has a historical feel and mainly refers to women who worked in factories during the industrialization period. For women at work today, people say '여성 노동자' or '여직원' instead.

examples.en: I replaced the water purifier's filter with a new one.

examples.ko: 수족관 여과기가 고장 나서 물이 흐려졌어요.
examples.en: The aquarium filter broke, so the water became cloudy.

examples.ko: 커피 여과기에 종이를 깔고 가루를 넣어요.
examples.en: I put paper in the coffee filter and add the grounds.

examples.ko: 여과기를 한 달에 한 번 씻어 주세요.
examples.en: Please wash the filter once a month.

examples.ko: 이 여과기는 작은 먼지도 잘 걸러 줘요.
examples.en: This filter catches even small particles of dust.
Food got stuck in the sink strainer.

explain: 물이나 공기, 커피 속의 찌꺼기를 걸러 내는 기구예요. 말할 때는 '필터'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It is a device that strains out residue from water, air or coffee. In speech people also call it a '필터'.

examples.en: My younger sibling is absorbed in preparing for the exam.
The kids are completely absorbed in their game.
Mom was fully occupied with washing the dishes.

examples.ko: 요즘 회사 사람들은 새 제품 홍보에 여념이 없어요.
examples.en: These days, people at the company are busy promoting the new product.

examples.ko: 비 오는 날에도 농부들은 일에 여념이 없어요.
examples.en: Even on rainy days, the farmers are hard at work.

examples.ko: 그는 책 읽기에 여념 없이 앉아 있었어요.
examples.en: He sat there absorbed in reading his book.

explain: 거의 '~에 여념이 없다' 모양으로 써서, 한 가지 일에 푹 빠져 다른 생각을 할 틈이 없다는 뜻이 돼요. '바쁘다'와 달리 그 일에 몰두하는 모습에 초점이 있고, 앞에는 몰두하는 일을 '-에'로 붙여요.

phrases.en: The students are busy with graduation preparations.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단어를 따로 풀면 뜻이 잘 안 잡히지만, 이 굳은 표현으로 '한 일에 몰두하다'가 돼요. 주로 글이나 뉴스에서 많이 나와요.
phrases.nuance_en: The word alone does not reveal this meaning, but this set phrase means being engrossed in one task. It is common in writing and news.

explain_en: It is almost always used as '~에 여념이 없다', meaning someone is so absorbed in one thing that they have no room for other thoughts. Unlike '바쁘다' (busy), it focuses on being immersed in the task, and the task is marked with '-에' before it.

examples.ko: 여행에서 돌아와서 하루 종일 여독을 풀었어요.
examples.en: I came back from the trip and spent all day recovering from travel fatigue.

examples.ko: 여독 때문에 오늘은 하루 종일 피곤해요.
examples.en: I'm tired all day today because of the trip.
The fatigue after a long flight is severe.
I want to relieve my travel fatigue at a hot spring.

examples.ko: 어머니가 여독에 좋은 차를 끓여 주셨어요.
examples.en: My mother brewed a tea that's good for travel fatigue.
I hadn't shaken off my travel fatigue, so going to work was hard.

explain: '여독을 풀다'가 가장 흔한 짝말이에요. 시차 때문에 생기는 피로와 달리, 여행길 전체에서 쌓인 피로를 말해요.
explain_en: '여독을 풀다' (to shake off travel fatigue) is the most common pairing. Unlike the tiredness caused by jet lag, it refers to the overall fatigue built up on the journey.

examples.en: In autumn, the grain ripens plump and full.
The chestnuts are fully ripe, so they taste good.
I picked a well-ripened pumpkin and made porridge.

examples.ko: 아이가 어른스럽게 여물어 가는 것 같아요.
examples.en: The child seems to be maturing and growing up.
The spring fruit hasn't fully ripened yet.
I wait until the seeds are fully formed.

explain: 열매나 곡식에는 '익다'보다 알맹이와 씨가 단단하게 꽉 찬 상태를 강조해요. 그래서 '여문 밤'처럼 속이 알찬 것에 잘 어울려요. ㄹ이 빠져서 '여문, 여무니, 여뭅니다'가 되고, 사람에게 쓰면 속이 단단하고 야무지게 자란 모습을 말해요.
explain_en: For crops and fruit, it stresses the kernel or seed filling out firm, whereas '익다' stresses becoming ready to eat. That is why it suits things that are solid inside, like '여문 밤'. The ㄹ drops, giving '여문, 여무니, 여뭅니다', and said of a person it describes someone who has grown up solid and capable.

examples.en: I packed a spare set of clothes in my bag.
If you happen to have a spare, please lend me one.

examples.ko: 비가 올까 봐 여벌로 우산을 하나 더 가져왔어요.
examples.en: I brought one more umbrella just in case it rains.
I made one extra copy of the key.

examples.ko: 여행 갈 때 여벌의 양말도 꼭 챙기세요.
examples.en: Be sure to pack extra socks when you travel.

examples.ko: 여벌이 없어서 젖은 옷을 그대로 입었어요.
examples.en: I had no spare, so I kept wearing the wet clothes.

explain: 입을 옷이나 쓸 물건을 갈아입거나 대신 쓰려고 따로 하나 더 마련한 것을 말해요. '여벌 옷', '여벌 신발', '열쇠 여벌'처럼 옷이나 신발, 열쇠 같은 물건과 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is something extra set aside as a change or replacement, such as clothes or an item. It pairs well with things like clothes, shoes and keys, as in '여벌 옷', '여벌 신발' and '열쇠 여벌'.

examples.en: Women's groups welcomed the new bill.
Figures from women's circles gathered for a meeting.
The voice of the women's community is getting louder.

examples.ko: 이번 정책에 대해 여성계가 입장을 밝혔어요.
examples.en: The women's community stated its position on this policy.
She is a person respected in women's circles.
Women's groups and the government have started talks.

explain: 뉴스나 신문에서 여성 문제와 관련된 단체와 인사들을 한데 묶어 말할 때 써요. '정계, 재계, 문화계'처럼 '-계'가 붙어 어떤 분야의 사람들 전체를 가리키는 말과 같은 틀이에요.
explain_en: It appears in news and newspapers to group together organizations and figures involved in women's issues. It follows the same pattern as '정계', '재계' and '문화계', where '-계' refers to everyone in a particular field.

examples.ko: 그 원피스는 여성미를 잘 살려 줘요.
examples.en: That dress brings out your femininity well.
She has a gentle, feminine charm.

examples.ko: 저는 여성미보다 편한 옷이 더 좋아요.
examples.en: I prefer comfortable clothes over looking feminine.
It's a photo where the actress's feminine beauty stands out.
This design emphasizes femininity.
I fell for her voice, full of feminine charm.

explain: 여성스러운 매력이나 아름다움을 말하고, 짝말로 '남성미'가 있어요. 사람마다 기준이 다르니 다른 사람에게 직접 말할 때는 조심하는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: It refers to womanly charm or beauty, and its counterpart is '남성미'. People's standards differ, so it's best to be careful about saying it directly to someone.

examples.en: Riding the momentum of their victory, they reached the final.

examples.ko: 우리 팀은 여세를 몰아서 다음 경기도 이겼어요.
examples.en: Our team kept the momentum and won the next game too.

examples.ko: 이 여세로 올해 목표를 이루고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to achieve this year's goal riding this momentum.
That team has tremendous momentum from its winning streak.

examples.ko: 여세를 몰아 숙제를 끝까지 다 했어요.
examples.en: I kept up the momentum and finished all my homework.

examples.ko: 그 가수는 인기 여세를 이어서 새 앨범을 냈어요.
examples.en: The singer kept up her popularity and released a new album.

explain: '여세를 몰아(서)' 모양으로 거의 쓰여서, 좋은 일이 있은 뒤의 기세를 타고 다음 일을 밀어붙인다는 뜻이에요. 대체로 승리나 성공처럼 긍정적인 흐름에 써요.

phrases.example: 어제 이긴 여세를 몰아 오늘도 이겼어요.
phrases.en: Riding yesterday's win, we won again today.
phrases.nuance_ko: '몰다'의 본래 뜻과 달리, 좋은 기세를 놓치지 않고 계속 이어 간다는 비유로 굳은 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike the original sense of '몰다' (to drive), this is a set figurative phrase for keeping a good momentum going.

explain_en: It is used almost entirely as '여세를 몰아(서)', meaning to ride the energy after something good and push on to the next thing. It usually applies to positive flows such as victory or success.

examples.en: A female flight attendant handed out drinks on the plane.

examples.ko: 여승무원은 안전 교육을 꼭 받아야 해요.
examples.en: Female crew members must receive safety training.
My friend passed the exam to become a flight attendant.
The female crew members greeted us with smiles.
I asked the female train attendant for directions.
When I was little, my dream was to be a flight attendant.

explain: 비행기나 열차에서 일하는 여성 승무원을 가리키지만, 성별을 따로 밝힐 필요가 없으면 그냥 '승무원'이라고 해도 돼요. 같은 틀로 '남승무원'도 있어요.
explain_en: It refers to a woman working as crew on a plane or train, but if you don't need to mention gender, simply saying '승무원' is fine. The same pattern gives '남승무원' for men.

examples.en: My daughter entered university this year.

examples.ko: 저희 여식이 늘 신세를 지고 있어요.
examples.en: My daughter is always indebted to you.
This child is my daughter.

examples.ko: 어르신 앞에서 여식 자랑을 해서 부끄러워요.
examples.en: I'm embarrassed to have bragged about my daughter in front of an elder.
I have one daughter, and she's a doctor now.

examples.ko: 여식을 먼 곳으로 보내는 마음이 복잡해요.
examples.en: I have mixed feelings about sending my daughter far away.

explain: 어른이나 윗사람에게 자기 딸을 낮추어 말하는 격식 있는 표현이에요. 남의 딸은 '따님'이라고 높이고, 평소에 가족끼리 말할 때는 그냥 '딸'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is a formal, humble way to refer to your own daughter when speaking to an elder or superior. Someone else's daughter is honored as '따님', and in ordinary family talk people simply say '딸'.

examples.ko: 이 사진은 그날 분위기를 여실하게 보여 줘요.
examples.en: This photo shows the atmosphere of that day vividly.

examples.ko: 소설 속 묘사가 너무 여실해서 무서웠어요.
examples.en: The description in the novel was so lifelike that it scared me.
His tiredness showed clearly on his face.

examples.ko: 여실한 묘사 덕분에 장면이 눈앞에 그려져요.
examples.en: Thanks to the vivid description, the scene comes to life before my eyes.
This video conveys the situation at the scene realistically.
A painting is more moving when it looks real.

explain: 실제와 같이 생생하게 드러나거나 그려진다는 느낌이고, 글이나 뉴스에서 자주 만나요. '여실히 보여 주다', '여실히 드러나다'처럼 부사 모양으로도 써요.
explain_en: It conveys something being shown or depicted as vividly as in real life, and you often meet it in writing and news. It also appears as an adverb, as in '여실히 보여 주다' and '여실히 드러나다'.

examples.ko: 병을 앓고 나서 얼굴이 많이 여위었어요.
examples.en: After being ill, her face became very thin.

examples.ko: 요즘 밥을 못 먹어서 점점 여위어 가요.
examples.en: I can't eat these days, so I'm growing thinner.
Seeing his thin shoulders made my heart ache.
Grandmother has grown so thin that I'm worried.
The cat was thin, but its eyes were bright.
You look worn thin because of hard work.

explain: 병이나 고생 때문에 몸이 마르고 약해 보일 때 써서, 날씬해졌다는 칭찬과 달리 걱정하는 느낌이 있어요. 활용은 '여위어요, 여위었어요, 여윈'으로 해요.
explain_en: It is used when someone gets thin and looks frail from illness or hardship, so it carries a worried feeling, unlike a compliment about being slim. The forms are '여위어요, 여위었어요, 여윈'.

examples.ko: 요즘 형편이 여의찮아서 여행은 못 가요.
examples.en: My finances are tight these days, so I can't go on a trip.
We provide support money to people in difficult circumstances.
If it isn't convenient for you, it's fine to come next time.
Things aren't going well, and I'm upset.

examples.ko: 지금은 시간이 여의찮은데 내일 얘기해도 될까요?
examples.en: I don't have the time right now, so can we talk tomorrow?
Their family situation seems difficult, and I'm worried.

explain: 형편, 사정, 일정이 뜻대로 되지 않을 때 돌려서 부드럽게 말하는 표현이에요. 정중하게 거절하거나 사정을 밝힐 때 '여의찮아서', '여의찮으시면'처럼 많이 써요.
explain_en: It is a soft, indirect way of saying that your finances, circumstances or schedule are not working out as you'd like. It helps in politely declining or explaining a situation, as in '여의찮아서' and '여의찮으시면'.

examples.en: The village women were gathered by the well.

examples.ko: 사극에 나오는 여인네의 옷이 정말 예뻐요.
examples.en: The clothes of the women in historical dramas are really pretty.

examples.ko: 여인네 한 명이 시장에서 나물을 팔고 있었어요.
examples.en: A woman was selling wild greens at the market.
A rumor spread among the women.
That woman walked away with a child on her back.

examples.ko: 할머니가 옛날 여인네들의 삶을 말해 주셨어요.
examples.en: Grandmother told me about the lives of women in the old days.

explain: 약간 옛스럽고 격식 없는 느낌이 있어서 사극, 소설, 옛날이야기에서 자주 만나요. 요즘 말로는 '여자분들'이나 '여성'이라고 하고, 지금 앞에 있는 사람에게 쓰는 건 피하는 게 안전해요.
explain_en: It has a slightly old-fashioned, informal feel, so you often meet it in historical dramas, novels and old tales. In modern speech people say '여자분들' or '여성', and it is safer not to use it for a person right in front of you.
